answer: To resist Sybil attacks, an agent economy can require every identity to stake a refundable deposit that grows with the number of identities one operator controls, like carving a distinct marble for each seat in a grove: every new marble costs real capital, and misbehavior burns it. Reputation then accrues only through verified, paid work over time, so an attacker who echoes the same cheap identity a thousand times gains nothing, since each echo must pay its own stake and earn its own history before it can transact.
